successCriteria.description: The validation module exposes a public entry point at src/modules/validation/index.ts that re-exports the ValidationResult model and the validation service (interface + implementation), mirroring the balance module's export shape.
Date-range validation rejects any input where startDate > endDate with a typed ValidationError (400), and accepts startDate <= endDate (including equal dates, which count as one day).

Inclusive day counting is performed by importing and calling the existing requestedDays(startDate, endDate) helper from src/shared/types/index.ts — never re-derived, re-exported, or aliased — so a same-day range yields 1 and an N-day span yields N.

Balance-sufficiency checking computes entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays and rejects with a typed ConflictError (409) when that remainder is less than the requested day count, and passes when it is greater than or equal.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/validation/ covering inclusive day counting (same-day, multi-day, cross-month) and sufficiency (sufficient, exactly-sufficient, insufficient) using in-memory fakes.

constraints: Import and call requestedDays directly from src/shared/types/index.ts; do NOT define a new helper, do NOT re-export it as calculateRequestedDays, and do NOT alias it — the canonical helper already exists there (Phase 1) and re-deriving it violates the 'implement ONCE' rule.
Use strict TypeScript with no `any`; use `unknown` plus type guards where needed (HARNESS.json no-any constraint).
Use relative imports (../../shared/types, ../../shared/errors, ../balance) and import only through the public index.ts entry points — never from module internals.

Follow the balance module's split-file layout: validation.model.ts, validation.service.ts, and index.ts, with the service interface declared alongside its implementation in the same file (no separate .interface.ts files).
Validation is a pure rules module: no audit writes, no routes/controllers, no RBAC, and no database access in this phase.
outOfScope: Audit-log writes (GP-002) — validation is a pure rules module; audit side effects are owned by the Phase 6 leave orchestrator.
HTTP routes, controllers, and RBAC enforcement — deferred to Phase 6.
Policy max-duration enforcement (maxConsecutiveDays / maxRequestDays) and notice-period (minNoticeDays) checks — not part of this phase's three required behaviors.
Any persistence/repository layer for the validation module — validation operates on in-memory inputs (DTOs and LeaveBalance) and performs no database access.

entityInvariants.invariant: A ValidationResult is a pure value object that reports whether validation passed and the list of failure reasons; it must never perform side effects or throw — the service decides whether to surface a typed error from it.
Sufficiency is derived solely from the balance's counters as entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays; the validation module must not mutate the balance or reinterpret OPEN/CLOSED state.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects startDate > endDate with ValidationError (400); accepts startDate <= endDate.
Rejects with ConflictError (409) when entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays < requestedDays; passes otherwise.
Composes date-range validation and sufficiency checking against the request's leave type balance; surfaces ValidationError (400) for invalid ranges and ConflictError (409) for insufficient balance.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The inclusive day count must be obtained by importing and calling the canonical requestedDays(startDate, endDate) helper — never re-derived — so every consumer (sufficiency, balance deduction, policy max-duration) uses the identical derivation.
Error semantics must reuse the shared AppError subclasses: ValidationError (400) for invalid input and ConflictError (409) for insufficient balance, matching the { error, code } contract.
The LeaveBalance shape consumed for sufficiency must match the canonical model (entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays counters) exported from the balance module's public entry point.
The sufficiency formula entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays >= requestedDays must match the canonical business rule so validation agrees with the balance module's own unused-day computation.

integrationPoints.why: Provides LeaveTypeCode, CreateLeaveRequestDto, and the canonical requestedDays helper the validation service consumes.
Provides ValidationError (400) and ConflictError (409) for the validation service's typed failure semantics.
Provides the LeaveBalance model whose counters drive the sufficiency check.
